text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- European share prices follow Wall Street's climb as dollar continues rising and U.S. consumer prices show modest increase.
-- French budget deficit at end-february at 72.4 billion francs, against 90 billion for February 1996.
-- European Monetary Insititute chairman Alexandre Lamfalussy expresses "cautious optimism" over single currency but says the "ratio of government deficit to GDP averages well over four percent".
-- European Space Agency ex-chairman Jean-Marie Luton seems set to become the next chief of Arianespace.
-- March European automobile sales down three percent.
-- Generale des Eaux increases stake in cinema group UGC to 40 percent from 33 percent.
-- Talk among members of ruling coalition continues on idea of cabinet reshuffle.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Peugeot and Renault lose market share in March as Citroen shows slight increase while Volkswagen and Fiat remain the two leading carmakers on the European auto market.
-- Finance ministry confirms commitment to cut public deficit to three percent this year and to 2.8 percent in 1998.
-- Paris would prefer Michel Camdessus to Wim Duisenberg for the chairmanship of the future European central bank.
-- Guinea-Bissau to join franc zone on May 2. Gambia and Guinea-Conakry may follow suit.
-- Beijing seems set to announce 10 billion franc Airbus order and 100-seater development deal during President Jacques Chirac's upcoming visit to China.
L'AGEFI
-- Lamfalussy says single currency should go into effect without waiting for more countries to qualify and that qualifying criteria should not be applied strictly in every case.
-- Thomson privatisation may not occur until September.
-- Credit Suisse First Boston says France Telecom is worth 169 to 195 billion francs.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Dollar climbs to 5.83 francs, up 12 percent since January.
-- OECD sees tough time for Italy to will qualify for single currency at the outset on January 1 1999.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- European Union agrees to cut fishing quotas despite dissenting votes of France and United Kingdom.
-- Paris seeking to win top European central bank post.
LE PARISIEN
-- Citroen to cut 800 jobs by September 1998.
-- Twenty-one percent of French consumers think Japanese products are good or excellent.
